newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orogen shares sparkle as year ends.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orogen shares sparkle as year ends.

text.p: Shares in mining investor Orogen Minerals Ltd continued their steep climb of the last fortnight to touch a record high of A$3.00 as investors sought exposure to the Papua New Guinean resources sector.
The shares have risen 15 percent from its close of A$2.61 on December 17 and since listing on November 1, 1996 at A$2.05 have rocketed 46.3 percent.

With a series of positive announcements since listing, including the government go-ahead for the Gobe oilfield and promising results from the Moran exploration well, buoying investor interest in the stock, brokers said investors were looking for the easy way to gain Papuan New Guinean exposure.
"It gives the best exposure to PNG of any stock," said dealer Duncan Gamble of Wilson HTM, adding that the mix of interests held by Orogen simplified the investment choice.
"You get exposure to the oil and the gold in the one stock without having to spread your assets around."
The Gobe oilfield, of which Orogen is to hold 20.5 percent, is located close to the existing Kutubu export pipeline and is expected to deliver an initial 50,000 barrels of crude a day.

Orogen, which is 51 percent-owned by the PNG government and which owns that country's mineral resources development division, offered 118.85 million shares in its float prospectus with retail investors paying A$1.70 per share and institutional investors another 30 cents per share.
Orogen has a stake in some of PNG's largest gold and petroleum projects including the Kutubu and Gobe oilfields and the Porgera, Misima and Lihir gold mines.
By 12.50 p.m. (0150 GMT), Orogen shares had eased from their highs to be four cents up at A$2.93 on turnover of 245,591 shares.
